title: Introduce lazy provider init and regional plugin registry to reduce Terraform plan time
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: CI and local developer 'terraform plan' latency for cross-region networking changes has regressed over time due to eager provider initialization, increased provider plugin matrix, and legacy networking templates that trigger provider discovery for every workspace. This ticket proposes introducing a lazy provider init flow along with a regional plugin registry and a small compatibility shim so terraform runs avoid unnecessary provider plugin downloads and initialization during plan phases when not required.

Goals: Reduce average terraform plan time for cross-region networking PRs by >=40% in CI and cut local plan latency for common workflows (subnet or route changes) by >=30%. Make provider init behavior opt-in via workspace-level config, and add a regional plugin registry to serve pre-cached provider binaries for our CI and build nodes.

Scope:
- Add a terraform wrapper that defers 'terraform init -get' until modules that actually require plugin interaction are invoked (lazy-init).
- Implement a small registry service (cached storage + signed metadata) that hosts vetted provider plugin binaries per region and exposes a canonical URL for using in providers_installation configuration.
- Update networking templates to declare provider installation metadata so they can opt into regional registry usage.
- Provide migration steps and CI changes (self-hosted runners and GHA) to use registry URLs.
- Add observability: measure plan duration, provider-init time, cache hit rate, and CI bandwidth savings.

Non-goals: Rewriting all modules or changing provider versions globally. Full provider upgrade matrix is out-of-scope for this ticket and will be tracked separately.
acceptance_criteria: CI terraform plan median time for networking PRs reduces by >=40% measured over 2-week window
Local developer 'make plan' for common subnet change reduces by >=30% on standard dev-machine spec
Regional plugin registry returns signed metadata and artifacts; registry 95% cache-hit on CI runs
Backward-compatible: existing workspaces continue to function without changes if they do not opt into lazy-init or registry
Documentation and migration guide published in Confluence and linked in the ticket
risks: Provider lifecycle edge-cases where lazy-init hides version mismatches until apply
Registry availability impacting CI — mitigation: fallback to public provider downloads
Security: hosting provider binaries requires signing and integrity verification to avoid supply-chain risk
rollout_plan: Prototype wrapper and registry in dev environment (week 1)
Integrate with CI runners, enable for low-risk repositories behind a flag (week 2)
Measure metrics, iterate on cache policies and TTLs (week 3)
Gradual opt-in across networking repos and infra teams, deprecate eager-init flag after adoption (week 4)
migration_steps: Add provider_installation config to module root pointing at regional registry URL
Toggle lazy-init flag in repo-level infra settings and run 'make plan' to validate
For CI: update self-hosted runner image to include registry CA and wrapper script
Monitor metrics dashboard and rollback flag if abnormal failures detected
comments: 2025-03-02 — Maya Chen: Spiked a prototype wrapper that defers 'terraform init' unless provider_installation metadata is present. Local tests show ~35% plan improvement for a single-region route change.
2025-03-04 — Liam O'Rourke: Benchmarked CI runner using a mocked registry — cache hit 88% on first run mix, plan latency median down from 22s to 12s across sample PRs.

2025-03-06 — Security (Priya Patel): Reviewed supply-chain concerns; require signed provider artifacts and attestation metadata. Added requirement to acceptance criteria for signed metadata verification.
2025-03-09 — Infrastructure (Diego Ramos): Running a small Canary of registry in us-west-2; observed sporadic 503s when cold-starting. Planning to add warm-up jobs and a small regional replica set.
